content:
When Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out: the all-new Siri Recap and a significantly improved heart rate monitor. While those were part of the reason I picked up the new Apple Watch, I found there was much more to get excited about.

Battery and Charging

While Apple's website doesn't list any additional battery life gains for the Apple Watch Series 12 over the Series 11, the battery life genuinely feels longer. As I've written before, prior to getting the Apple Watch Series 12, I was a WHOOP user and, although the Apple Watch stayed by my side, I never used it for sleep tracking.

After the keynote, I decided to give Apple Watch sleep tracking a try. That said, on my Series 11, juggling both sleep tracking and charging was a bit of a hassle. After wearing the watch all day, I'd have to charge it before bed, and then charge it again after waking up.

The Series 12 doesn't have that problem. Its battery life gets me through a full day plus an entire night, and I now charge it after I wake up. The Apple Watch Series 12 also charges noticeably faster, making charging far less of a chore. According to Apple, a 15-minute charge provides up to 12 hours of use.

I suspect the new S11 chip (a derivative of the 2nm A20 Pro design) is the main reason the battery life feels dramatically extended. Regardless of the reason, it's a relief to be free of charging anxiety caused by sleep tracking on the Apple Watch Series 12. Another big selling point of the S11 chip? The Apple Watch Series 12 feels much snappier, especially when using Siri.

Software Exclusives

The Series 12 finally adds a proper step counter as a watch face complication, which I enjoy viewing in the Smart Stack. Will this feature trickle down to older Apple Watches? Possibly. Apple has actually been counting steps all along, but the Series 12 is notably more accurate. Since the data is already there, I think Apple should just go ahead and add the complication. Either way, it's great to have it on the Series 12.

Another new feature worth mentioning is the all-new Readiness app, which gives you a sense of how you're doing today based on your sleep the night before, your activity levels from the previous day, and your vitals. It's similar to WHOOP's recovery score, and I'm of course glad Apple has brought this to the Apple Watch. Unfortunately, it's a Series 12 exclusive, which is a bit of a shame, though I understand Apple not wanting to do the calculations on less accurate data.

The Verdict

All in all, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a pretty solid upgrade. While it's not a major redesign 'S year,' if what you care about is the Apple Watch actually doing more, rather than just looking different, this might be the most meaningful year-to-year upgrade since the Apple Watch Series 4.

Compared to the Series 10 and 11, the bezels are indeed very slightly thicker. As someone who uses a black background watch face, I don't really notice it, but I'd love to see Apple improve this with the next generation.

One more thing worth noting: the Apple Watch Series 12 brings Ceramic Shield 2 glass to the aluminum case models, giving them dramatically improved scratch resistance over older Apple Watches. While I haven't owned the watch long enough to truly test this, my Apple Watch is still pristine so far.

My favorite Apple accessories:

  • Anker Ultra-Slim MagSafe Battery Pack
  • AirPods Pro 3 (twice the active noise cancellation of the AirPods Pro 2!)
  • Anker Nano 45W Smart Display Charger
  • Anker Prime 3-in-1 25W Compact MagSafe Charger
  • Logitech MX Master 4 for Mac
  • AirTag 2 4-Pack (Precision Finding improved by 50%!)
  • Belkin 3-in-1 MagSafe iPhone Charging Stand
  • MOFT MagSafe iPhone Stand Wallet
